Component variations that define different visual styles, behaviors, and configurations. Each variant type can be combined to create the desired component appearance.

## Component Name

Brief description of the component and its role in the interface.

### Type Variants

Content structure configurations that determine the layout and visual presentation format of the component.

<CxVariant img="component-name-type-basic">

#### Basic

Description of this type variant and when to use it.

</CxVariant>

### Style Variants

Visual presentation modes that affect the component's appearance within the interface.

<CxVariant img="component-name-style-solid">

#### Solid

Description of solid style variant and when to use it.

</CxVariant>

<CxVariant img="component-name-style-smooth">

#### Smooth

Description of smooth style variant and when to use it.

</CxVariant>

<CxVariant img="component-name-style-outline">

#### Outline

Description of outline style variant and when to use it.

</CxVariant>

### Context Variants

Semantic or color variations that communicate different meanings or importance levels.

<CxVariant img="component-name-context-default">

#### Default

Description of default context and when to use it.

</CxVariant>

<CxVariant img="component-name-context-primary">

#### Primary

Description of primary context and when to use it.

</CxVariant>

Different scale variations to support various layout needs and information hierarchies.
